description: Randomized topics from your 30-topic list • Fresh content only

cards.title: Cleaner Energy Adoption
cards.passage: Many countries are trying to reduce pollution by using cleaner forms of energy. Solar power and wind power are becoming more popular every year. However, some people still prefer traditional fuels because they are cheaper in the short term. Governments offer money to help families install solar panels on their roofs. Scientists believe these changes can help protect the planet for future generations.

questions.question: What do governments provide to encourage the use of solar energy?

options.A: Free electricity for households that continue using traditional fuels
options.B: Financial support for families to install solar panels
options.C: Lower prices for traditional fuels to keep them competitive
options.D: Immediate guarantees that the planet will be fully protected

questions.question: All countries have completely stopped using traditional fuels.
Solar power and wind power are becoming more ________ every year.
What do scientists believe these energy changes can help protect?

cards.title: The Growth of Online Education
cards.passage: Online courses allow students to study from home at any time. Many universities now offer recorded lectures and interactive quizzes. Some learners still prefer classroom lessons because they enjoy talking with teachers. Schools sometimes give extra help to students who study online. Good internet connection is important for successful online learning.

questions.question: Why do some students prefer classroom lessons?

options.A: They dislike recorded lectures and interactive quizzes
options.B: They enjoy direct interaction with teachers
options.C: They find online courses always easier than classroom ones
options.D: They never need extra help when studying online

questions.question: All universities offer recorded lectures for every course.
Good internet connection is important for successful online ________.
What do many universities now offer?

cards.title: Smartphones and Social Connection
cards.passage: Smartphones help people stay connected with family and friends. Many apps allow users to share photos and messages instantly. Some older people find new technology difficult to learn. Companies regularly update their apps to make them easier to use. Young people often spend many hours on their phones every day.

questions.question: Why do companies regularly update their apps?

options.A: To make them more difficult for older people
options.B: To make them easier to use
options.C: To reduce the number of hours people spend on phones
options.D: To stop users from sharing photos and messages

questions.question: All older people find new technology easy to learn.
Smartphones help people stay connected with family and ________.
What do many apps allow users to share instantly?

cards.title: Benefits of Regular Physical Activity
cards.passage: Regular exercise is important for keeping the body strong and healthy. It can also help people feel happier and less stressed. Some people exercise at home while others prefer going to a gym. Doctors often recommend thirty minutes of activity most days. Eating fruit and vegetables is also good for overall health.

questions.question: What benefit does regular exercise provide besides physical health?

options.A: It always increases stress levels
options.B: It can help people feel happier and less stressed
options.C: It guarantees perfect health without any other changes
options.D: It replaces the need to eat fruit and vegetables

questions.question: All doctors recommend exactly thirty minutes of exercise every day.
Regular exercise is important for keeping the body strong and ________.
What do doctors often recommend?

cards.title: The Impact of Social Media
cards.passage: Social media allows people to share ideas with friends around the world. Many users post photos and videos every day. Some people worry that too much social media can cause stress. Families sometimes spend more time on phones than talking to each other. Governments are now creating rules about online safety for children.

questions.question: What concern do some people have about social media?

options.A: It completely prevents sharing ideas with friends
options.B: Too much use can cause stress
options.C: It always improves family conversations
options.D: It has no effect on children’s safety

questions.question: All families spend more time on phones than talking.
Social media allows people to share ideas with friends around the ________.
What are governments creating rules about?

cards.title: Global Trade and Local Businesses
cards.passage: Global trade has increased rapidly because of better transportation and communication. Companies can now sell products to customers in many different countries. However, some local businesses struggle to compete with large international companies. Governments sometimes introduce taxes to protect local industries. Economists continue to study the effects of globalization on employment.

questions.question: What challenge do some local businesses face?

options.A: Complete protection from all international competition
options.B: Difficulty competing with large international companies
options.C: Guaranteed growth due to better transportation
options.D: Automatic tax benefits for every local industry

questions.question: All governments introduce taxes to protect local industries.
Economists continue to study the effects of globalization on ________.
What has increased rapidly because of better transportation?

cards.title: New Developments in Medical Treatments
cards.passage: Scientists are developing new medicines to treat diseases that were difficult to cure in the past. Clinical trials are necessary to ensure these medicines are safe for patients. Some new treatments use advanced technology such as gene editing. However, these treatments are often very expensive. Researchers hope that costs will decrease as technology improves.

questions.question: Why are clinical trials necessary for new medicines?

options.A: To make the treatments more expensive for patients
options.B: To ensure the medicines are safe for patients
options.C: To completely avoid the use of gene editing
options.D: To guarantee that costs will never decrease

questions.question: All new treatments using gene editing are already affordable.
Researchers hope that costs will decrease as technology ________.
What are scientists developing to treat difficult diseases?

cards.title: Green Spaces in Urban Areas
cards.passage: Many large cities are building more parks and green spaces to improve air quality. These areas also provide places for residents to relax and exercise. However, high land prices make it difficult to create new parks in central areas. City planners are now designing vertical gardens on building walls. Local communities often help maintain these green spaces.

questions.question: What challenge do city planners face when creating new parks?

options.A: Complete absence of any land price issues
options.B: High land prices in central areas
options.C: Guaranteed automatic maintenance by all residents
options.D: Reduced need for vertical gardens on buildings

questions.question: All large cities have successfully built enough parks.
City planners are designing vertical gardens on building ________.
What do many large cities build to improve air quality?

cards.title: Challenges of Renewable Energy Transition
cards.passage: The transition to renewable energy sources continues to face technical and economic challenges despite significant investment. While solar and wind capacity has grown substantially, the intermittent nature of these sources still requires advanced storage solutions. Some analysts suggest that current policy incentives may not sufficiently address grid stability concerns. Long-term decarbonisation targets depend on both technological breakthroughs and consistent political support.

questions.question: What do some analysts suggest about current policy incentives?

options.A: They have fully resolved all grid stability concerns
options.B: They may not sufficiently address grid stability concerns
options.C: They guarantee immediate technological breakthroughs
options.D: They eliminate the need for any political support

questions.question: Policy incentives have already ensured long-term grid stability for all renewable sources.
Long-term decarbonisation targets depend on both technological breakthroughs and consistent ________ support.
What continues to face technical and economic challenges?
questions.correctAnswer: the transition to renewable energy sources

cards.title: Artificial Intelligence in Decision-Making
cards.passage: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into workplace decision-making processes has raised questions about accountability when algorithmic recommendations lead to unintended consequences. Although many organisations claim that regular audits can minimise bias, critics argue that underlying training data often reflects historical inequalities. Achieving genuine fairness may require more than technical adjustments. Public trust in these systems remains fragile despite growing adoption.

questions.question: What do critics argue about the training data used in AI systems?

options.A: It is always completely free from historical inequalities
options.B: It often reflects historical inequalities
options.C: It eliminates the need for any accountability measures
options.D: It guarantees perfect fairness in all recommendations

questions.question: Regular audits have fully resolved all bias issues in workplace AI systems.
Achieving genuine fairness may require more than technical ________.
What has raised questions about accountability in workplace AI?

cards.title: Workplace Mental Health Initiatives
cards.passage: Workplace mental health initiatives have gained prominence as organisations recognise their link to long-term productivity. However, many employees still hesitate to seek support due to perceived career risks associated with disclosure. Flexible working arrangements have helped some staff, yet persistent cultural stigma continues to limit uptake. Comprehensive policy reform is widely regarded as essential for meaningful progress.

questions.question: What continues to limit employee uptake of mental health support?

options.A: Complete absence of any perceived career risks
options.B: Persistent cultural stigma surrounding disclosure
options.C: Guaranteed career benefits from seeking support
options.D: Automatic removal of all flexible working options

questions.question: Flexible working arrangements have eliminated all barriers to mental health support.
Many employees still hesitate to seek support due to perceived career ________ associated with disclosure.
What have workplace mental health initiatives gained?

cards.title: Biodiversity Loss in Tropical Regions
cards.passage: Accelerating biodiversity loss in tropical ecosystems is now understood to involve complex feedback loops that amplify the effects of habitat fragmentation. While some conservation programmes report localised recovery, the overall trajectory suggests that many species face extinction risks that exceed previous modelling estimates. Economists increasingly highlight the undervaluation of ecosystem services in national accounting systems. Global funding mechanisms have expanded, yet disbursement efficiency remains a persistent challenge.

questions.question: What do economists increasingly highlight regarding ecosystem services?

options.A: Their full and accurate valuation in all national accounting systems
options.B: Their undervaluation in national accounting systems
options.C: Their complete irrelevance to biodiversity loss
options.D: Their automatic protection through all conservation programmes

questions.question: Global funding mechanisms have achieved optimal disbursement efficiency across all projects.
The overall trajectory suggests that many species face extinction risks that exceed previous modelling ________.
What is now understood to involve complex feedback loops?

cards.title: Sustainable Development Challenges
cards.passage: The pursuit of sustainable development goals has revealed significant tensions between economic growth targets and environmental protection priorities in many developing nations. Although international frameworks emphasise integrated approaches, implementation often prioritises short-term economic gains over long-term ecological stability. Some reports suggest that current progress indicators may understate the true extent of environmental degradation.

questions.question: What do some reports suggest about current progress indicators?

options.A: They fully capture the true extent of environmental degradation
options.B: They may understate the true extent of environmental degradation
options.C: They have no connection to economic growth targets
options.D: They guarantee long-term ecological stability in all nations

questions.question: International frameworks have resolved all tensions between economic growth and environmental protection.
Implementation often prioritises short-term economic gains over long-term ecological ________.

questions.correctAnswer: the pursuit of sustainable development goals

cards.title: High-Speed Rail Development
cards.passage: High-speed rail networks are increasingly viewed as essential components of sustainable urban mobility strategies. However, the substantial upfront capital costs and long construction timelines continue to deter many governments from full commitment. Some studies claim that the economic returns may take decades to materialise, particularly in regions with lower population density. Public-private partnership models are frequently proposed as a solution, yet their long-term viability remains debated.

questions.question: What do some studies claim about the economic returns of high-speed rail?

options.A: They materialise immediately in all regions
options.B: They may take decades to materialise, especially in lower-density areas
options.C: They eliminate the need for any public-private partnerships
options.D: They have no relation to population density

questions.question: Public-private partnership models have proven fully viable for all high-speed rail projects.
The substantial upfront capital costs and long construction timelines continue to deter many governments from full ________.
What are high-speed rail networks increasingly viewed as?
questions.correctAnswer: essential components of sustainable urban mobility strategies

cards.title: Precision Agriculture Technologies
cards.passage: Precision agriculture technologies promise to optimise resource use while maintaining or increasing crop yields. Nevertheless, the high initial investment and technical expertise required often limit adoption among small-scale farmers in developing regions. Some research indicates that the environmental benefits may be partially offset by increased energy consumption from advanced equipment. Global food security strategies increasingly incorporate these technologies, yet equitable access remains a critical unresolved issue.

questions.question: What does some research indicate about the environmental benefits of precision agriculture?

options.A: They are always fully realised without any drawbacks
options.B: They may be partially offset by increased energy consumption
options.C: They eliminate the need for any technical expertise
options.D: They guarantee immediate adoption by all small-scale farmers

questions.question: Precision agriculture technologies have resolved equitable access issues worldwide.
Global food security strategies increasingly incorporate these technologies, yet equitable ________ remains a critical unresolved issue.
What do precision agriculture technologies promise to optimise?

cards.title: Television versus Streaming Services
cards.passage: Television remains a popular source of news and entertainment for many families. People can watch programmes from different countries on their televisions. Some families prefer streaming services because they can choose what to watch. Advertisements on television help companies sell their products. News channels provide information about events happening around the world.

questions.question: Why do some families prefer streaming services?

options.A: They dislike watching programmes from different countries

questions.question: All families prefer streaming services over traditional television.

cards.title: Managing an Aging Population
cards.passage: Many countries now have more older people than in the past. This change creates more demand for healthcare services. Some older people continue working because they enjoy their jobs. cards.title: Space Tourism by Private Companies
cards.passage: Private companies are now sending tourists into space for short periods. These trips offer passengers amazing views of Earth from above. options.D: Automatic development of international rules without cost issues

cards.title: Preserving Cultural Traditions
cards.passage: Many countries work hard to preserve their traditional festivals and customs. Young people sometimes prefer modern entertainment to old cultural events. cards.title: Improving Waste Management through Recycling
cards.passage: Recycling programmes help reduce the amount of waste sent to landfills. Many cities now have separate bins for different types of rubbish. options.C: They develop new sorting technology for companies

cards.title: Data Analytics in Professional Sports
cards.passage: Professional athletes increasingly rely on data analytics to optimise training regimes and reduce injury risk. While these tools provide valuable insights, some coaches argue that over-dependence on metrics may diminish the role of intuitive coaching decisions. options.C: They guarantee perfect injury prevention in every case

cards.title: Predictive Policing Algorithms

options.A: It is always free from any historical inequalities

cards.title: Climate Diplomacy Negotiations

cards.title: Digital Media and Human Behavior
cards.passage: The digital transformation of social interaction has been linked to measurable changes in attention spans and emotional regulation among younger generations. While some researchers suggest that these shifts are primarily adaptive, others contend that prolonged screen exposure may contribute to heightened anxiety levels. The causal relationship remains difficult to isolate amid numerous confounding variables.

questions.question: What do some researchers suggest about the shifts in attention and emotional regulation?

options.B: They are primarily adaptive

cards.title: Recent Archaeological Discoveries
cards.passage: Recent archaeological discoveries have challenged long-held assumptions about the technological capabilities of ancient civilisations in remote regions. While some findings suggest advanced engineering knowledge, others indicate that these achievements may have been more localised than previously thought. cards.title: Alternatives to Animal Testing
cards.passage: The ethical debate surrounding animal testing in medical research has intensified with the development of sophisticated alternative testing methods. Although some scientists claim that these alternatives can fully replace animal models, others maintain that certain complex biological responses still require living organisms. cards.title: The Fast Fashion Industry
cards.passage: Fast fashion business models have been criticised for contributing to excessive textile waste and exploitative labour practices. cards.title: The Rise of the Gig Economy
cards.passage: The gig economy has transformed traditional employment relationships by offering greater flexibility for workers while reducing long-term job security.
